items.edit: Mütze und Fliege aus dem früheren Festporträt auf Porträt und Posen des regulären Plüschhasen gelegt.
Die Gesichtspartie der Jubelpose aus b08027c an derselben Stelle eingesetzt. Die sichtbaren Pixel der anderen sieben Posen stimmen mit dem vorherigen Export überein.
Gewickelte Hände und geschlossener Kopfverband wie auf der Bühne. Neles gezeichnete Augen sitzen unter den Öffnungen der Bandagen.
Schwarzes Oberteil, schimmernder taupefarbener Rock, Armwickel und Federkopfschmuck. Gesichtspartien aus der regulären Iset. Der zweite Laufschritt erhielt eine eigene Gegenbewegung.
Naturfarbenes Kleid mit Kordelgürtel, wenige Halme in den Locken, Holzschwert und nackte Füße. In der Hängepose greift die Hand um den Schwertgriff. Gesichtspartien aus Johannas Anno-Figur.
Rotes Cape, dunkle Rüstung und braune Riemenschuhe nach der Bühne. Gesichtspartien aus derselben Anno-Figur wie beim Strohkleid.
Die WebP-Datei und alle sieben Seilpunkte stammen byte- bzw. koordinatengleich aus b08027c. Das vorhandene Porträt und Kartenbild entsprechen ebenfalls dieser Fassung.

Für die einzige Anno-Figur von Logge dienten ihr ursprüngliches Porträt und das Bühnenfoto als Referenzen. Leon aus Anno gab die Malweise vor. Der Bote aus Creepshow diente ergänzend als Gesichtsvergleich.
Partymaskierung und Rock der bisherigen Variante, lange gestreifte Bluse nach der regulären Motte. Der Bund überdeckt die Bluse auch beim Hängen, Fliegen und Liegen. Jule ist die Darstellerin.

prompts.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. ONE full body running animation cel for a theatre game on real transparent background, facing and travelling to the RIGHT. Image 1 is the existing Iset ball dress for identity and consistent clothing, golden shoes, long mushroom-pink-beige skirt, black bodice, gilded sash, white arm wraps, flowing chestnut hair with black feather/gold masquerade mask up on hair. Image 2 is the final sheet for rendering and costume. Draw the OPPOSITE contact phase to that sheet's top left. The NEAR arm swings FORWARD across the front of her chest, elbow bent, clearly visible wrapped forearm and fist in front of the gold collar toward the right; far arm swings backward past hip toward left, only partially visible behind torso. Near knee and lower leg drive BACK toward left, near gold sandal tucked high behind; far knee goes up visibly forward, the far sandal reaching right. A different flowing S-shaped fold in the soft ball skirt reveals these two distinct different leg positions. Adult Nele's original side-view face, features and settled running expression, high quality warm painterly shading and thin brown contour matching the existing portrait, tiny black shoulder harness with a small theatre strap fitting. No fan, extra stuff, text, floor or shadow. One isolated complete figure, transparent margin around raised feather and both feet.

Use case: identity-preserve. Image 1 is Nele's ORIGINAL established Creepshow Iset model, the edit target. Image 2 is for the ballroom costume and stage-harness fit only. Image 3 is the actual COSTUME on stage at left: dark sleeveless bodice with Egyptian gold collar, broad metallic gold sash and long draped, pale muted greige/mushroom-satin skirt; ivory fabric wraps on the ARMS to below the shoulders, gold flat strapped sandals. Image 4 is this same actor's variant portrait for the filigree gold mask resting UP ON HER HAIR and the little black feather, leave face fully visible. Re-dress character 1 in that costume through all eight poses preserving the exact shape of her forehead, brows, long nose, calm eyes, cheeks, chin and long, individually drawn dark chestnut flowing hair, height, broad gestures and proportions. Remove the original fan. Maintain the SAME warm, richly painted theatre game art as image 1 with delicate tapered dark umber lines, graded light on skin/hair/fabric. Preserve adult age and face at smaller scale, no big grinning child or oversized fluttery eyelashes. Skirt hangs in long, heavy fluid folds, reacts to strides. Consistent narrow gold center sash panel; mask sits on HEAD above forehead and black feather rises from it in every pose. Arrange in exactly 4 columns 2 rows in same order, facing right: four distinct consecutive run phases (near leg ahead, passing with leg down, opposite leg ahead, opposite passing with knee high); cheer arms up, dangling seated, stretched horizontal flight then prone horizontal crash with tiny dizzy stars. Same feet lower line in first row. Truly transparent background, each full body completely separate with gaps. No boxes, crop, lettering, floor or thick sticker borders.

Use case: identity-preserve. Keep exactly her individual face from image 1, warm original theatre-game paint and fine dark-brown contours, with hand-painted highlights on hair and the fabric of skirt, as in image 2. Use case: identity-preserve costume edit. Image 1 is the original hand-painted JOHANNA game model of Elena in Anno 1146, the edit target for identity, figure and eight poses. Image 2 shows her knight costume in matching poses and required small sheathed sword on belt. Image 3 is the real stage COSTUME only. Paint a finished coherent costume-variant sheet for image 1 in the identical warm, fine brown-line Anno storybook-game rendering. Keep her specific side profile, upturned brows, eyes, ear, nose, jaw, skin, abundant individual dark chestnut ringlets with warm highlights and their exact silhouette, body proportions and expressive gestures. The knight wears a red wool cape fastened at throat with gold clasp, flowing BEHIND the shoulders, blouse in warm ivory with wide gathered sleeves, brown cuffs and broad waist cincher, dark near-black slim leggings, small practical leather thigh straps, dark strap sandals, single sheathed stage sword at hip. Use the real cloth, silhouette and folds evident in image 3. No full metal armor. Match the anatomy, exact order and orientation of image 1 in 4 columns by 2 rows: wide run, passing, opposite wide run, opposite passing; cheer, seated suspended dangle, horizontal fly, face-down horizontal crash with two tiny stars. Run legs alternate. Fine ink, modeled shadows and hair, not heavy black vector outlines. Keep each head in the position, size and facing direction of the source pose, all hands clear, no extra characters, props or outlines. One whole body per cell, generous clear space. Single wide transparent sheet, no ropes, floor, scenery, labels or border.

Use case: identity-preserve costume edit. Image 1 is the original painted Johanna portrait of Elena in her knight outfit, editing target. Preserve her exact head shape and size, sideways gaze, eye/eyebrow placement, mouth, nose, striking dark brown ringlets, neck, hands on belt, and painterly warm storybook technique. Use case: style-transfer. Production 2D TheaterApp sprite sheet, exactly eight isolated full bodies of ONE theatre actor in 4 equal columns x 2 rows, wide landscape, real transparent background. Image 1 is the FINAL painted portrait of the character Logge in Anno 1146: carry face identity, hair, tunic dye, fold rendering to every frame. Image 2 is the SAME man's previous GAME POSES and costume. Image 3 is the standard GAME SHEET from the SAME PRODUCTION, for the painterly storybook rendering, head scale, athletic articulated limbs, soft ochre highlights and dark umber tapered contours. Do not copy the third character, hair or axe. Depict Logge, modest adult grin, short curly dark-blond hair, little cheek creases; avoid squinting/smiling during flight or dangling as if posing for camera. Narrow detailed woven trim, red long-sleeve tunic belted with a black belt, dark charcoal ankle trousers, bare undamaged feet, small round dark metal stage-harness fitting flush behind shoulder. Top left to right: right-facing RUNNING wide split near leg ahead, PASSING pose one leg straight and other bent at knee, opposite wide stride, opposite passing. Bottom left to right: cheerful arms overhead standing tall, dangling seated legs hanging frightened, stretched rightward horizontal flight, flat horizontal crash facing right with two small illustrated golden dizzy stars. Use the order and gestures of image 2, and the weight, body proportions, silhouette/shading complexity of image 3. Natural foot soles, individual hands, all facing right. Do not add weapons, props, large metal loops, black outer stroke, flat vectors, oversize mugging eyes or caption. Preserve generous transparent gaps around/between figures, keep fly and crash in bottom columns 3 and 4. No stage, platform, shadows, dividers or type.

Use case: style-transfer and identity-preserve. Production transparent 512x512 wardrobe card (generate high resolution square). Repaint this specific male actor as the Anno 1146 ENSEMBLE villager, in the same illustrator's hand as the established neighboring cards. Image 1 is the existing Logge Anno portrait for his individual identity, head angle, friendly modest grin, narrow angular chin, clear light eyes, short wavy dark-blond hair and the red costume. Image 2 is an established Anno 1146 painted card for rendering/method only, never that man's face, ax, blue costume or hair. Image 3 is Logge's established drawn facial likeness only, ignore the cap and delivery costume. Image 4 is the actual stage costume reference only. Red, long-sleeved, simple woven tunic, modest V-neck with narrow patterned edging, black belt, tiny glimpse of black trousers; black narrow stage harness with small buckles as in the cards. Fair adult face with natural cheek planes and smile creases; painted strands along temples, not solid fills, relaxed eyes and a recognisable nose. Rich warm theatrical storybook-game illustration, graduated shadow in cloth folds, fine warm brown contour subtly varying in weight, warm bounced light against cooler red fold shadows, same ink-and-paint detail and face scale as image 2. No flat outlined comic shapes, exaggerated grin, big bobble head, stubble if absent, points, magic or equipment. No axe, no broom, no staff. Single waist-up three-quarter composition, hands gently at waist; 5% headroom over hair, cropped at lower hips at bottom only. Genuine transparent background, no vignette, labels, frame or other figures.

Use case: identity-preserve. Image 1 is the FINAL Motte (Partyoutfit) portrait and the definitive costume model: full-length lavender pinstriped button blouse, long sleeves, button cuffs, tucked deeply into broad opaque black waistband. Trace that exact unbroken join between purple fabric and black skirt around her entire body. Her waist and back are ALWAYS fully covered with cloth, in every pose including stretched flight or lying down. Image 2 supplies EIGHT FULL-BODY POSES and layout ONLY. Replace its short top entirely with image 1's long-sleeve blouse. In the two horizontal poses the waistband must overlap the purple blouse by several centimeters at the back; the view from the side shows continuous purple cloth meeting black with absolutely NO skin-colored band, ocher line, light gap, exposed lower back, navel or ties. Flesh only on face, fingers and any legitimately exposed shins. Same theatre masquerade mask, feather, long dark curls, black skirt with multicolour patchwork inset and boots. Match her expressive face in each source pose. Eight fully separated clear silhouettes on an ACTUAL TRANSPARENT ALPHA canvas, no white matte, no shadow, no particle, no labels, no floor or frame. Four columns/two rows, order exactly top alternating wide run, passing, opposite run, opposite passing; bottom cheer, dangle, horizontal fly right, horizontal face-down crash with eyes closed/dizzy cartoon expression and yellow stars. Give each enough empty transparent gutter, keep the character scale constant. Match drawing style and waist geometry of the FIRST portrait; use second only for placement and pose.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Production EDIT of image 1, the EXISTING eight animation frames of Motte (Partyoutfit), played by Jule. Image 2 is her established same-play Motte skin for blouse tailoring only, not a competing face or hairstyle. Image 3 is her party card for identity and skirt. Change only her top. Give Motte a proper full-length softly striped dusty-lilac button-front blouse, gently loose, with her classic collar, long sleeves and buttoned cuffs as in her established Creepshow costume. All of the cloth is TUCKED INTO the waistband of her EXISTING black party skirt so it stays closed over stomach and back in every movement, including with both arms high. No bare midriff, cutout, knotted/cropped hem or belly tie. Keep mask in place over eyes, the delicate feather, her original loose dark chestnut curls, face, skin tone, head, harness webbing, boots, and black skirt with small burgundy/ochre/teal patchwork inset. Do not add her everyday black overalls. Match the target full bodies' exact height, face, expressions, anatomy, silhouettes, orientations, hand positions and foot positions. Four poses wide on top (rightward run, pass, opposite run, opposite pass), then cheer with both arms high, seated dangle, horizontal fly, horizontal crash with small dizzy stars. One clear full-body image per cell, generous transparent gutters. True transparent background; no captions, floor, effects or thick outline.
